name: E-commerce fraud prevention
one_line: Decides in milliseconds whether an online order is a real buyer or a thief, and often eats the loss if it guesses wrong.
sells: Real-time fraud scoring for online orders, usually priced per transaction or as a share of approved sales, often with a chargeback guarantee
customers: Online retailers, marketplaces and the payment processors that serve them
suppliers: Cloud computing, consumer identity and card-network data, device signals, machine-learning talent

revenue.note: Global Market Insights' payment-fraud segment; the whole fraud-detection & prevention market was ~$36.6B in 2025. The specialized e-commerce transaction / chargeback-guarantee vendors shown here are a smaller, fragmented subset of this: Riskified, the only public pure-play, booked $345M in FY2025.

structure.why: Dozens of specialist vendors compete, none with real scale: Global Market Insights reports the five largest fraud-detection vendors held just 7.58% of the market combined in 2025. The e-commerce niche splits further into independents (Riskified, Signifyd, Forter) and fraud tools bundled inside bigger platforms (Stripe, American Express, Equifax).
structure.hhi_note: Shares are not published on a comparable revenue basis, so no HHI is computed. GMI reports the top five fraud-detection vendors held a combined 7.58% in 2025, implying a very low HHI (a highly fragmented market).

econ: Information asymmetry. At checkout a seller cannot tell a genuine shopper from a fraudster, so it is stuck choosing between turning away good customers and eating fraud losses. These vendors pool transaction data across thousands of merchants to price each order's risk, and many guarantee the chargeback, turning an unknowable risk into a predictable fee the seller pays.
rank_basis: estimated annual revenue (Riskified official FY2025; the private firms are third-party estimates, 2024-2025)

companies.name: Riskified
companies.note: The only public pure-play (NYSE: RSKD). Reviewed $155B of GMV in 2025, up 10%; revenue is a risk-adjusted fee on the GMV it approves.

companies.name: Signifyd
companies.note: Private; revenue is a third-party estimate (GetLatka). Last valued ~$1.3B (2021 Series E, $390M raised to date).

companies.name: Forter
companies.note: Private; revenue is a third-party estimate (Growjo $110.6M; GetLatka $103M). Reportedly valued around $3B after its 2021 round.

companies.name: Sift
companies.note: Private; revenue is a low-confidence third-party estimate. Sells a broad 'Digital Trust & Safety' suite, not only chargeback guarantees.

companies.name: Sardine
companies.note: Private; revenue is a third-party estimate. Spans fraud and anti-money-laundering, aimed at fintechs and instant payments as well as commerce.

companies.name: Stripe Radar
companies.note: Fraud scoring built into Stripe's payments; not separately disclosed, but reaches millions of merchants by default. An embedded competitor, not an independent vendor.

companies.name: Accertify
companies.note: Owned by American Express; enterprise fraud and chargeback platform. Revenue folded into Amex, not disclosed.

companies.name: Kount
companies.note: Owned by Equifax; fraud and identity-trust platform. Revenue folded into Equifax, not disclosed.

products_note: Flagship product lines as of Nov 2026, checked against each vendor's own site and recent coverage. Private-company revenues are third-party estimates (GetLatka, Growjo, NewMarketPitch), clearly marked; only Riskified's figure is from a filing.
